AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818)
937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is
discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance,
please contact the Library, Arts and Culture Department, at (818) 548-2030, during regular business
hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  JULY 20, 2023 AT 10:00 AM

  1.  REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA – 10:00 AM
  Roll Call

  2.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the May 18, 2023 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting
 3.  INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes.
  Members of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.

5.  WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

  6. ACTION ITEMS
  a. Mural Ordinance and Program – Community Meeting and Program Strategy
  1. Motion approving the Director of Library, Arts & Culture to enter into a Professional
  Services Agreement in an amount not to exceed $5,050 from the 2023-2024 Work Plan
  — with Beautify Earth, a creative services consultant, to (1) review the draft mural
  ordinance and policies and procedures and provide feedback, (2) host a community
  meeting on the mural ordinance, and (3) work with GLAC staff and Arts and Culture
  Commission to define strategy and best approaches for mural program processes and
  execution.
  b. Adams Hill Arts Festival - Programming and Sponsorship Opportunity
  1. Motion approving (1) the funding of an event management company and artist
  stipends associated with the Adams Hill Arts Festival, and (2) the sponsorship of the
  Adams Hill Arts Festival, in an amount not to exceed $3,000 from the 2023-2024 Work
  Plan.
  c. Glendale International Film Festival - Programming and Sponsorship Opportunity
  1. Motion approving (1) the funding of a proposal by Glendale Arts to provide arts
  programming associated with the Glendale International Film Festival, and (2) the
  sponsorship of the Glendale International Film Festival, in an amount not to exceed
  $5,000 from the 2023-2024 Work Plan.
  d. Ex-Officio Student Non-Voting Member of the Arts and Culture Commission –
  Selection Committee
  1. Motion selecting two Commission members to serve on an ad hoc Ex-Officio Student
  Non-Voting Member Selection Committee (Selection Committee), to conduct the
  screening and selection of qualified candidates for interviews.

7.  DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2023-2024 Work Plan Progress Updates

8.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

9.  ADJOURNMENT
  The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is Thursday, August
  17, 2023, at 10:00 AM in City Council Chambers.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, May 18, 2023, at 10:00 a.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on May 18, 2023, at 10:04 a.m.
  •  Present: Commissioner Vidor, Yank, Chairperson Viar
  •  Absent: Commissioner Tufenkian, Commissioner Zadorian
  •  The Agenda for the May 18, 2023, Regular Meeting was posted on May 18, 2023, on the Bulletin
  Board outside City Hall.

2. CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or the
  audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the March 16, 2023 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting (Approved as
  Amended)

  Moved:  Commissioner Yank
  Seconded :  Commissioner Vidor

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Commissioner Yank, Chairperson Viar
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Tufenkian, Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

  b. Minutes of the April 5, 2023 Special Arts and Culture Commission

  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded :  Commissioner Yank

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Commissioner Yank, Chairperson Viar
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Tufenkian, Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

3. INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones,
  Principal Arts & Culture Administrator
  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts &
  Culture locations.

4. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS- NONE

  1
 5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes. Members of
  the Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the Speaker, but there will be no Debate or
  Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
  – NONE

6. ACTION ITEM(s)
  a. City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ – Design Concept Proposals for Central Park Ground level
  Artwork
  1. Motion recommending that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter into an Agreement
  for Commission of Artwork an artist/artist team to design, fabricate, and install a public art piece for
  the Central Park Ground level Artwork in an amount not to exceed $100,000 dispersed from the
  2023-2024 Work Plan.

  •  Dr. Shaffer stated that the proposed public art piece will be located on the northeast section
  of the park that is being replanned for Central Park and not adjacent to a planned Armenian
  American Museum.
  •  Bo Basse, of LeBasse Projects gave a brief update on the RFQ -Design concept proposals.
  •  Commission asked questions and gave their input. Dr. Shaffer also gave his input.
  •  Arsan, a member of Gegham Abrahamyan team called in and gave a summary of their
  proposed project.

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby recommends that the City Council authorize the City
  Manager, or a designee, to enter into an Agreement for Commission of Artwork with one of the
  artists/artist teams listed below to design, fabricate, and install a public art piece for the Central
  Park Ground level Sculpture in an amount not to exceed $100,000 dispersed from the Urban Art
  Program Fund, as more fully outlined in the May 18, 2023 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s
  Principal Arts & Culture Administrator:

  First Recommendation: Gegham Abrahamyan, for the artwork entitled, “Reality Series.”
  Alternate Recommendation: Pneuhaus, for the artwork entitled, “Interlaced.”

  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded :  Commissioner Yank

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Commissioner Yank, Chairperson Viar
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Tufenkian, Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

  b. City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ #2 – LeBasse Projects
  1. Motion approving the proposed locations for public art landmark pieces to be included as part of the
  City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ #2, and the application review process to be managed by
  LeBasse Projects on behalf of the City of Glendale.

  •  Bo Basse, of LeBasse Projects gave a brief update on the proposed locations for public art
  landmark pieces.
  •  Commission asked questions and gave their input. Dr. Shaffer also gave his input.

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby approves the proposed locations for public art
  landmark pieces to be included as part of the City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ #2, and the
  application review process to be managed by LeBasse Projects on behalf of the City of Glendale,
  as more fully outlined in the May 18, 2023, Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts &
  Culture Administrator.
  2
   Moved:  Commissioner Yank
  Seconded :  Commissioner Vidor

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Commissioner Yank, Chairperson Viar
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Tufenkian, Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

7. DISCUSSION ITEM(s) / REPORT(s)
  a. 2022-2023 Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Mural Ordinance – Update
  • Staff is working with Ms. Odenkirk on drafting a Mural Ordinance in addition to Policies
  and Procedures which will complement the Mural Ordinance. The draft Mural Ordinance
  and Policies and Procedures will be scheduled for initial review by the Commission at an
  upcoming Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.

  ii. City-Wide Public Art – Update
  On February 17, 2022, during the Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission,
  the Commission approved the 2022-2023 Work Plan which details the use of funds to
  administer activities during this time frame. The following updates are programs from the
  Work Plan that have had recent activity.

a. CITY WIDE ARTS
  i.  Mural Ordinance – Update:
  • Staff is working with Ms. Odenkirk on drafting a Mural Ordinance. The final draft Mural
  Ordinance and Policies and Procedures will be scheduled for initial review by the
  Commission at the June Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission.
  ii.  City-Wide Landmark Public Artworks – Update:
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones briefly went over six of the public landmark locations starting with
  Verdugo Park Ground level/Building Mural Piece. Staff is in the process of working with
  Ms. Wray and are anticipating installing the mural in October 2023.
  • Central Park Ground Level Sculpture Staff stated that three locations are still under
  discussion due to the potential redesign of the street but include: Artsakh Ave. Gateway
  Public Art Piece, Artsakh Ave. Overhead Public Art Piece and Artsakh Ave. Ground level
  Sculpture
  • Glenoaks Blvd. / Brand Blvd. Median Sculpture: Staff is in talks with Water and Power in
  regard to the fabrication and foundation for that particular artwork.

  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS-
  • Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station Exhibits – Update
  • Staff met with Vice-Chair Tufenkian and Commissioner Zadorian for the Artist Review &
  Selection Committee to discuss applications for the Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station
  exhibits. Staff received 35 applications for consideration. Ms. Loreto shared the
  programming recommendations selected by the selection committee.
  • Commissioner Vidor asked for status regarding Creative Crosswalks Mural on Adams and
  Palmer. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that will be installed potentially sometime in July and
  stated Staff would get an update from Public Works. She stated that other two Creative
  Crosswalk Murals on Broadway and Columbus and Broadway and Galleria Way would be
  potentially installed in June.

  3
   3. PERFORMING ARTS – No Update
  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update
  5. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS
  • PR Firm – Update
  On May 9, 2023, during the Regular City Council Meeting, City Council authorized the City
  Manager, or a designee, to enter into and execute a Professional Services Agreement—
  subject to approval by the City Attorney— with The ACE Agency, Inc. Staff is in the
  process of working with The ACE Agency to establish an agreement and begin a strategic
  plan for marketing and communications in the next couple of weeks.

8. COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS
  •  Commission thanked Staff for all the input, progress and work they do.
  •  Commissioner Yank stated that there is an upcoming fund called Art in the Parks; Parks California is
  administering. Commissioner Yank talked about Landscaping and Park planning and mentioned the
  Diversity and Equity policy and thinking around the Native First peoples of this region, with Parks with
  land acknowledgement at programs and stated there should be more consulting with the tribes that
  have ancestral claims to this land. She suggested having tribal biologists be part of the discussions in
  terms of what types of landscaping and native plants and what kind of access they can have for culture
  and ceremonial purposes, and that it is a cultural concern as well as a parks and landscaping concer
  and she would be happy to be part of discussions. Dr. Shaffer said Staff would share thoughts with
  Parks Department.
  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that on May 9th the Glendale Library Arts and Culture Trust (GLACT) is a
  Grantee for the Getty Pacific Time and Standard Initiative Art & Science Collide. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones
  stated that GLACT will be partnering with JPL on a project called “The Stars Collide” and it will be
  slated for Fall of 2024 through early spring of 2025; The exhibit will take place at the Brand Library.
  •  Dr. Shaffer stated that staff is in talks with Artist Shepard Fairey to potentially exhibit at Reflect Space
  and potential talks of having a Shepard Fairey mural in Glendale.

9. ADJOURNMENT 11:27 a.m.
The next Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is June 15, 2023, at 10:00 a.m., in City Council
Chambers (2nd Floor), 613 E. Broadway.
